Research log.name: panic_day_rebound
Research log.verdict: 2026-11-20 PROMISING (not proven): buy at the close when the market (SPY) falls 2%+, the stock falls 3%+ and is 15%+ below its 20-day high (CCJ Nov 5 2026 type). 61 distinct days since 2019: hold 4 days +3.6% avg / +3.3% median, up 62%; hold 6 days +5.3% / +6.2%, up 70% (p=0.001 by day), positive every year. Risk: when the panic is the start of a crash (Feb-Mar 2020, May 2022) it loses 15-21% and stops don't help (gaps). Buying next morning instead of the close keeps much less (+0.9% over 2 days). ~23 variants tried, so treat as a candidate for paper testing. | 2026-11-20 filters tried (first vs repeat panic, market vs 200-day avg, market drawdown, size of market/stock drop; 10 more trials): none removes the crash days cleanly, splits are 4-15 days and flip between halves. Kept the simple rule; protection = size (15% each, 45% total, 3 names). Now trading on paper as strategy #2. | 2026-11-20 round 3 (25 more trials): which 3 to pick barely matters (deepest-under-high +6.0% vs biggest-drop +5.3%, noise); VIX 40+ days best (+9.3%, 85% up, n=13); SECTOR-only panics have no edge (+0.6%), it needs the whole market; fixed 6-day hold best avg, but sell at +10% close or day 6 = +5.0% avg, 72% up, worst -17.5% (vs -21.4%) and frees cash sooner -> adopted. Non-panic swings: best is -10% in 3 days in a calm market, +2.1% over 6d vs +1.0% for any day, steady in both halves (practice candidate only).

Research log.name: ccj_daily_reversal
Research log.verdict: 2026-11-20: CCJ day-to-day moves are close to random (autocorrelation -0.02). After up/down days of 3-5%, 5-8%, 8%+ and gap-and-reverse days, the next 1-3 days show no reliable bounce-back (p 0.19-0.95). The 'jumps up then back down' pattern is visible but not predictable from the day's move alone; across all 10 stocks, company-only up spikes do fade (see big_move_followthrough).

Research log.name: panic_rebound_calls_estimate
Research log.verdict: 2026-11-20 ESTIMATE (Black-Scholes, implied vol = 1.3x recent vol on entry, 1.05x on exit, ~5% spread each way; no real historical option prices): 2-week calls on the panic-day picks turn the stock's +5.2% into about +5% (at the money) or 0% (5% out of the money) on average, median -9% to -16%, winning on <50% of days, losing 80%+ on 11-15%. Fear makes options expensive exactly on panic days. Shares beat calls for this setup. Re-test with the options recorder's real chains once enough panic days are recorded.
